at.description: The step that reveals the whole figure; shown from the start when left out.

caption.description: The measure, unit and period above the plot ("Tickets per month, 2026"); the slide title states the takeaway.

source.description: Where the data comes from, set under the plot.

label.description: The accessible name; built from the data when left out.

data.description: Rows inline (data={[...]}), imported from a JSON or CSV file in the deck folder, or the name of a dataset in the slide's `data:` frontmatter. Two rows for the same category (and series) throw.

highlight.description: What the chart is about. A series name, else a category (or max, min, first, last), several, or a `Highlight` object (see `types.Highlight`); everything else drops to the brand's context color. `at` turns it on at a step.

annotations.description: Callouts, reference lines, shaded ranges and brackets as objects with a `type` of `callout`, `reference`, `range` or `bracket`; their fields are under `types` as `Annotation.callout`, `Annotation.reference`, `Annotation.range` and `Annotation.bracket`. Each takes `at`.

format.description: How values are written, over the brand's number style (compact, its currency and locale). Percent values are already in percent: 34 is 34%. `digits` fixes the fraction digits; without it currency in full writes cents or none (never one decimal), and a value under 1 keeps a significant digit.

unit.description: The unit after each value: "ms", "°C", "h", "trees". A scale unit (K, M, B) sits tight and keeps a currency sign: unit="M" with currency writes $1.2M.

labels.description: Which values are labeled on the marks. `auto` labels every value when few enough to read (and drops the value axis), else the highlighted ones.

legend.description: Force the legend on or off. Charts label series directly and show a legend only when they cannot (grouped and stacked bars); with a highlight the legend names the highlighted series and "everything else".

value.description: The number, formatted by the brand, or text as it should read.

label.description: What it counts, in a few words.

delta.description: The change as written ("+12% since 2025"); computed from `from` when that is given.

from.description: The value it is compared with, for a computed delta.

relative.default: true; false for values in percent
relative.description: Write the change from `from` as a percentage of it, or in the unit (`false`). The default is a percentage, except for values in percent (unit "%" or format "percent"), whose change is written in points: "+7 pts". A change across zero is always written in the unit.

better.description: Which way is good news, for a computed delta.

tone.description: Whether the change is good news; from `better` and the sign when left out.

trend.description: Which way the change points, for a delta written without a sign.

spark.description: Recent values, oldest first, drawn as a sparkline under the label.

highlight.description: The stat the point rests on: an accent rule and the accent color.

format.description: How this stat's number is written, over the row's.

unit.description: This stat's unit, over the row's; it resets the row's format style unless it is a scale (K, M, B).

value.description: How far it has come; past `max` the track runs on and marks where the whole ended.

target.description: The goal, marked on the track.

unit.description: This bar's unit, over the figure's; it resets the figure's format style.

format.description: How this bar's numbers are written, over the figure's.

highlight.description: The bar the point is about, when there are several.

label.description: The header; the field name when left out.

format.description: How the column's numbers are written; exact (as many digits as the data has) when left out.

bar.description: Draw an in-cell bar to scale from zero.

align.description: The alignment; numbers right, text left when left out.

field.description: The field that holds the series' values.

label.description: The name the chart labels the series with; the field name when left out.

at.description: The step that reveals the series.

style.description: `percent` values are in percent already (34 is 34%); `currency` adds the currency sign.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 currency code, such as `EUR`.

digits.description: Exactly this many fraction digits, 0 to 4.

signed.description: Always show the sign, for changes: `+12`.

category.description: Categories to keep in color (or max, min, first, last).

range.description: A stretch of categories, `[first, last]`, both ends inclusive. On a line chart it covers the segments between consecutive highlighted points, so the line is drawn heavier and in color from the first category to the last; every segment outside it, including the one after the last category, stays muted. A range of one category colors no segment (use `category` for a single point).

at.description: The step that turns the highlight on; the chart shows its own colors before it.

by.description: What each step adds: one series, or one category, in data order.

from.description: The step the first one comes in at, a whole number of 1 or more (step 0 is the slide before any step); each next one comes a step later. Series with their own `at` keep it.

x.description: The category (a point name, on a Scatter) it points at.

label.description: The text, a few words: "Redesign ships".

series.description: The series whose point it marks; the highlighted or first series (on a Slope, the `to` field).

y.description: A value to point at instead of the series' value.

value.description: The value on the value axis.

label.description: The text at its end, such as "Target"; the formatted value is added after it.

from.description: The first category of the span.

to.description: The last category of the span.

from.description: The category of the first point.

to.description: The category of the second point.

series.description: The series; the highlighted or first series.

label.description: The text; the change between the two values when left out.

relative.description: Write the change as a percentage of the first value, or in the unit. A change across zero (or from near zero) is always in the unit.

better.description: Which way is good news, for the label's color.

charts.name: BigNumber
charts.useWhen: One number is the message ("we cut onboarding to 3 days"); it beats a chart of one or two bars.
charts.avoid: A number without the comparison that gives it meaning; add `from` or `context`.
charts.data: No rows: `value` (number or text), `label`, and `from` or `delta` for the change.

value.description: The number, formatted by the brand, or text as it should read ("3 in 10").

label.description: What it counts, in about six words.

context.description: The comparison in a line: "down from 14 days in 2025".

from.description: The value it is compared with; the change is written as the delta.

delta.description: The change as written, when not computed from `from`.

tone.description: Whether the change is good news; from `better` and the sign when left out.

better.description: Which way is good news, for the delta's color.

relative.default: true; false for values in percent
relative.description: Write the change from `from` as a percentage of it, or in the unit (`false`). The default is a percentage, except for values in percent (unit "%" or format "percent"), whose change is written in points: "+7 pts". A change across zero is always written in the unit.

trend.description: Recent values for a sparkline set against the figure.

charts.example: <BigNumber value={3} unit="days" label="from signup to a live workspace" from={14} better="down" relative={false} />
charts.accessibility: The figure, label, delta and context are text; the summary reads them in order.

charts.name: StatRow
charts.useWhen: Two to four headline numbers that belong together, each with its change and an optional sparkline.
charts.avoid: More than four numbers (use a Table) or numbers in different units that the audience must compare.
charts.nulls: No rows; each stat needs a `value`.

stats.description: Two to four stats; set `highlight: true` on the one the point rests on.

charts.example: <StatRow stats={[{ value: 38, unit: '%', label: 'fewer tickets', highlight: true }, { value: 2.5, unit: 'h', label: 'first reply', from: 14, better: 'down' }]} />
charts.accessibility: Every value and label is text; sparklines are decoration (`aria-hidden`) beside the numbers they trend.

charts.name: Comparison
charts.useWhen: Two values, before and after or A against B, where the difference is the message.
charts.avoid: Several items changing between two points: use Slope.
charts.data: No rows: `from` and `to`, each { value, label }. A value below zero is drawn from a zero line both bars share, towards the start edge, so a loss never reads as a gain.
charts.nulls: No rows; both values are required.

from.description: The value before, or the first.

to.description: The value after, or the second: the one the point is about.

relative.default: true; false for values in percent
relative.description: Write the change from `from` as a percentage of it, or in the unit (`false`). The default is a percentage, except for values in percent (unit "%" or format "percent"), whose change is written in points: "+7 pts". A change across zero is always written in the unit.

charts.example: <Comparison from={{ value: 14, label: '2025' }} to={{ value: 2.5, label: 'October 2026' }} unit="h" better="down" />
charts.accessibility: Both values, their labels and the change are text; the bars to scale are decoration.

charts.name: BarChart
charts.useWhen: Compare categories or rank them: sorted horizontal bars for long labels, columns for a few periods.
charts.avoid: One or two bars (use BigNumber or Comparison), or before/after for many items (use Slope).
charts.data: Rows with a category field and one or more number fields (wide), or category, series and value fields (long).
charts.nulls: A missing value draws no bar and no label; the category keeps its place. A chart with no values at all is reported by `deckster lint` (chart-empty).

x.description: The category field; the first text field when left out.

y.description: The value field or fields, one series each (see `types.SeriesInput`); `at` reveals a series at a step. Every number field when left out.

series.description: For long data, the field whose values name the series (then `y` is the one value field).

orientation.description: Columns or bars; `auto` turns horizontal when labels do not fit under columns.

stacked.description: Stack the series instead of grouping them.

sort.description: Sort by value, largest first for `true`; "Other" stays last.

min.description: The axis minimum: above zero only with `truncate` (drawn with an axis break, the value axis and an "Axis starts at" note); lint reports it otherwise.

truncate.description: Allow `min` above zero, with a break across every bar.

reveal.description: Build the marks in steps, one series or one category per step. A string starts at step 1; the object form (see `types.RevealOption`) starts at `from`, a later step.

charts.example: <BarChart data={regions} x="region" y="revenue" format="currency" sort highlight="EMEA" />
charts.accessibility: Named "Bar chart of <series> by <field>"; the summary gives each series' highest and lowest category and what is highlighted.

charts.name: LineChart
charts.useWhen: Change over time: one line, or one highlighted among muted context lines, each labeled at its end.
charts.avoid: More than about five lines without a highlight (spaghetti), two measures on two axes, or a single point (use BigNumber).
charts.data: Rows in time order with a time field and one number field per line (or long rows with `series`).
charts.nulls: A missing value breaks the line there (a gap, never a zero); a line that stops early is labeled where it stops.

x.description: The category field; the first text field when left out.

y.description: The value field or fields, one series each (see `types.SeriesInput`); `at` reveals a series at a step. Every number field when left out.

series.description: For long data, the field whose values name the series (then `y` is the one value field).

zero.description: Start the value axis at zero; otherwise it hugs the data and says where it starts.

reveal.description: Build the marks in steps, one series or one category per step. A string starts at step 1; the object form (see `types.RevealOption`) starts at `from`, a later step.

charts.example:
<LineChart data={tickets} x="month" y={['2025', '2026']} highlight="2026" annotations={[{ type: 'callout', x: 'Jun', label: 'Redesign ships' }]} />
Range highlight, muting the rest of the line: <LineChart data={tickets} x="month" y="2026" highlight={{ range: ['Jun', 'Sep'] }} />
charts.accessibility: The summary gives each line's first and last value and what is highlighted.

charts.name: AreaChart
charts.useWhen: A trend whose size matters (volume, backlog), or a composition over time when stacked.
charts.avoid: Comparing several series (use LineChart); only the bottom stacked series and the total read well.
charts.nulls: A missing value leaves a gap in its area; stacked, the stack breaks at that category for that series and every series above it (never drawn as zero).

x.description: The category field; the first text field when left out.

y.description: The value field or fields, one series each (see `types.SeriesInput`); `at` reveals a series at a step. Every number field when left out.

series.description: For long data, the field whose values name the series (then `y` is the one value field).

stacked.description: Stack the areas; put the series that matters first.

min.description: Ignored below zero: areas start at zero.

reveal.description: Build the marks in steps, one series or one category per step. A string starts at step 1; the object form (see `types.RevealOption`) starts at `from`, a later step.

charts.example: <AreaChart data={replies} x="week" y="hours" unit="h" annotations={[{ type: 'reference', value: 4, label: 'Target' }]} />

charts.name: Slope
charts.useWhen: Change between two points for several items: who rose and who fell, at a glance.
charts.avoid: Grouped bars for the same data; more than about ten items.
charts.data: Rows with an item field and two number fields (`from` and `to`).
charts.nulls: Every item needs both values: a missing one throws an error naming the item.

x.description: The category field; the first text field when left out.

from.description: The first value's field; the first number field when left out.

tone.description: Color items by better or worse instead of the lead color.

annotations.description: Callouts on a point (`type: 'callout'`, fields in `types['Annotation.callout']`) and reference lines across the plot (`type: 'reference'`, fields in `types['Annotation.reference']`); ranges and brackets throw here. Each takes `at`.

charts.example: <Slope data={teams} x="team" from="2025" to="2026" better="down" tone highlight={['Billing', 'Payroll']} />
charts.accessibility: The summary lists every item's two values.

charts.name: Donut
charts.useWhen: Part of a whole when one or two parts matter ("more than half"), five slices at most.
charts.avoid: More than five slices or close values (use sorted bars); two donuts side by side.
charts.data: Rows with a name field and a value field.
charts.nulls: A missing or negative value is a slice of zero: it draws nothing and counts as 0%.

x.description: The category field; the first text field when left out.

y.description: The value field; the first number field when left out.

centerLabel.description: The line under the centre figure.

charts.example: <Donut data={channels} x="channel" y="conversations" highlight="Chat" centerLabel="on chat" />
charts.accessibility: The summary gives the total and every slice's share.

charts.name: Pictogram
charts.useWhen: A proportion that should feel human: "3 in 10", risk, reach.
charts.avoid: Precise shares or totals above 100 units.

total.description: How many units there are, at most 100.

columns.description: Units per row; chosen from the room when left out (10 or 20 for totals divisible by ten).

charts.example: <Pictogram value={3} total={10} label="questions now end in the help centre" />

charts.name: Progress
charts.useWhen: Progress toward a goal, one bar or a short list, with the target marked.
charts.nulls: No rows; each bar needs a `value`. A value past `max` shows the overshoot.

value.description: How far it has come, for a single bar.

target.description: The goal, marked on the track.

label.description: What is measured, for a single bar.

charts.example: <Progress value={31} target={40} unit="%" label="of questions solved by self-serve" />
charts.accessibility: Every value, maximum and goal is in the summary.

charts.name: Waterfall
charts.useWhen: How a total builds up or breaks down between two totals (a bridge: last year to this year).
charts.avoid: A stacked bar with many colors.
charts.data: Rows with a step name and a change; total rows (named in `totals`) hold a level, or none for the running total.
charts.nulls: A total with no value is the running total; a change with no value counts as no change and is labeled "—".

x.description: The category field; the first text field when left out.

y.description: The change field; the first number field when left out.

totals.description: The steps that are totals; the first step when left out.

better.description: Which way is good news, for rises and falls ("down" for costs). Steps keep their tone colors; `highlight` mutes the changes it does not name, never the totals.

reveal.description: Build the bridge in steps: the totals and the step names show from the start, then `"categories"` brings in one change per step and `"series"` all of them at once. A string starts at step 1; the object form (see `types.RevealOption`) starts at `from`.

charts.example: <Waterfall data={bridge} x="step" y="cost" totals={['2025', '2026']} better="down" format="currency" />
charts.accessibility: The summary walks the steps from the first total to the last with every change.

charts.name: Funnel
charts.useWhen: Drop-off through ordered stages, where the share that carries on between stages is the point.
charts.avoid: Unordered categories (use BarChart), or stages that grow (`deckster lint` warns).
charts.data: Rows in stage order with a stage name and a count.
charts.nulls: A stage with no count draws an outlined "no data" slot, and the shares into and out of it are "—".

x.description: The category field; the first text field when left out.

reveal.description: Build the funnel in steps: `"categories"` brings in one stage per step with the share that carried on into it, `"series"` the whole funnel at once. A string starts at step 1; the object form (see `types.RevealOption`) starts at `from`.

charts.example: <Funnel data={journey} x="stage" y="people" highlight="Opened an article" />
charts.accessibility: The summary gives every stage's count and the share that carried on.

charts.name: Scatter
charts.useWhen: The relationship between two measures, with the notable points labeled and an optional trend.
charts.data: Rows with two number fields and a name field (and a group field for `series`).
charts.nulls: A row missing either value is left out.

x.description: The x field; the first number field.

y.description: The y field; the second number field.

label.description: The field naming each point, for highlights, callouts and labels (not the accessible name here).

series.description: The field grouping points into colored series.

xLabel.description: What x measures, at the end of the x axis.

yLabel.description: What y measures, at the top of the y axis.

xFormat.description: How x values are written (format and unit are y's).

trend.description: Draw the least-squares trend line, clipped to the plot.

annotations.description: Callouts on a point (`type: 'callout'`, fields in `types['Annotation.callout']`) and reference lines across the plot (`type: 'reference'`, fields in `types['Annotation.reference']`); ranges and brackets throw here. Each takes `at`.

charts.example: <Scatter data={squads} x="hours" y="csat" label="squad" trend highlight={['Billing']} xLabel="Hours to resolve" yLabel="Rated good, %" />
charts.accessibility: The summary gives the number of points, the trend's direction and the highlighted points with values.

charts.name: MarketMovement
charts.useWhen: One entity changes position over dated observations against peers on two fixed axes.
charts.avoid: Movement in only one measure (use LineChart) or a single snapshot (use Scatter).
charts.data: Long rows with an entity name, ISO calendar date and two numeric measures.
charts.nulls: A row missing either measure has no position. Peers appear only on their observation dates.

xFormat.description: The horizontal axis number format. The shared format is for y.

highlight.description: The entity whose positions form the trail.

buildFrom.description: The step for the second date. Each later date adds one step.

charts.accessibility: The static chart labels the trail endpoints. The summary lists positions by date.

charts.name: Heatmap
charts.useWhen: A pattern across two dimensions (weekday by hour), with the cell that matters outlined.
charts.avoid: Exact values to compare (use a Table).
charts.data: Long rows with a column field, a row field and a value field.
charts.nulls: A missing cell is drawn empty, outside the color scale.

highlight.description: Cells (or a whole row or column) to outline.

scale.description: The words at the ends of the scale legend.

charts.example: <Heatmap data={load} x="hour" y="day" value="tickets" highlight={{ x: '9–12', y: 'Mon' }} />
charts.accessibility: The summary gives the range and the highest cell; values are printed in cells with room.

charts.name: RetentionCohorts
charts.useWhen: Retention by signup cohort and elapsed age, with the starting populations beside the rates.
charts.data: Long rows with a cohort name, a whole elapsed age, a starting population and retention in percent.
charts.nulls: Absent or explicitly null rates stay blank. An observed zero is printed as 0%.

age.description: The elapsed age field, a nonnegative whole number.

ageUnit.description: The heading prefix for each age.

sizeLabel.description: The heading of the starting population column.

focus.type: { cohort: string; age: number; from?: number }
focus.description: Outline the cohort at `from`, then compare cohorts at `age` one step later. Leave out `from` for a static comparison at `age`.

charts.accessibility: The summary names the starting populations, observed rates and focus age. Blank cells are unobserved.

charts.name: ProfitPool
charts.useWhen: Segment revenue is a width and contribution margin a height, making area represent profit.
charts.avoid: Profit is the only measure that matters (use BarChart).
charts.data: One row per segment with positive revenue and a margin in percent. A margin may be negative.
charts.nulls: Revenue and margin are required to calculate profit. A zero margin has zero area.

revenue.description: The revenue field. All rows must use the same currency and scale.

margin.description: The contribution margin field. Pass 25 for 25%.

highlight.description: The segment to emphasize. Defaults to the largest profit contributor.

buildFrom.description: The margin step. Before it the chart shows revenue only, and the next step highlights profit.

charts.accessibility: The summary gives revenue, margin and profit for every segment.

charts.name: Sparkline
charts.useWhen: A trend as context beside a number, in an aside or a sentence; StatRow and BigNumber have their own.
charts.avoid: A trend that is the message (use LineChart).
charts.data: `values` (numbers, oldest first) or rows with one number field.
charts.nulls: A missing value breaks the line there.

y.description: The field of the rows to draw.

highlight.description: The point to mark and label.

value.description: Write the marked value at the end.

charts.accessibility: Summarised as its first and last value.

charts.name: Table
charts.useWhen: Exact values, lookups or mixed units, about five rows by four columns, with the row that matters emphasized.
charts.avoid: A pattern across many values (use a chart); the full dataset (put it in the appendix).
charts.data: Rows; `columns` picks and labels fields (see `types.TableColumn`). Numbers are written exactly (no rounding) unless a format sets `digits`; pass numbers, not text such as "31%", so they align and format.
charts.nulls: A missing cell is left empty.

columns.description: The columns in order; every field when left out.

highlight.description: Rows (by first-column text or index), a column or cells, marked the brand's way.

charts.example: <Table data={plans} columns={['plan', { key: 'cost', format: 'currency', bar: true }]} highlight={{ row: 'Team' }} />
charts.accessibility: A real table with header cells; the summary lists the rows.

insight.title: The slide title states the takeaway ("Tickets fell 38% after the redesign"); the chart proves it. Put the measure, unit and period in `caption`.
insight.props: Each chart takes the shared props its `shared` names and its own `props`; any other prop name throws an error naming the closest one ("`value` is not a prop of BarChart; did you mean `y`?").
insight.highlight: What the chart is about. A series name, else a category (or max, min, first, last), several, or a `Highlight` object (see `types.Highlight`); everything else drops to the brand's context color. `at` turns it on at a step.
insight.annotations: Callouts, reference lines, shaded ranges and brackets as objects with a `type` of `callout`, `reference`, `range` or `bracket`; their fields are under `types` as `Annotation.callout`, `Annotation.reference`, `Annotation.range` and `Annotation.bracket`. Each takes `at`.
insight.labels: Charts label directly (line ends, bar tips, slices) and show a legend only when they cannot.
insight.honesty: Bars and areas start at zero; a bar axis above zero needs `truncate` and draws a break, its value axis and an "Axis starts at" note. Lines may zoom and say where the axis starts.
insight.steps: `at` on a chart, on a series in `y`, on `highlight` and on each annotation reveals it at a step, from step 1 (step 0 is the slide before any step); `reveal` builds by series or category, and on a Waterfall builds the changes between totals that show from the start. The last step is the complete chart, which static mode and export show.
insight.data: Rows inline (data={[...]}), imported from a JSON or CSV file in the deck folder, or the name of a dataset in the slide's `data:` frontmatter. Two rows for the same category (and series) throw.
insight.nulls: Each chart's `nulls` says how it draws a missing value (null, an empty CSV cell, text that is not a number).
insight.format: How values are written, over the brand's number style (compact, its currency and locale). Percent values are already in percent: 34 is 34%. `digits` fixes the fraction digits; without it currency in full writes cents or none (never one decimal), and a value under 1 keeps a significant digit.
insight.relative: Write the change from `from` as a percentage of it, or in the unit (`false`). The default is a percentage, except for values in percent (unit "%" or format "percent"), whose change is written in points: "+7 pts". A change across zero is always written in the unit.
insight.limits: Each chart's `limits` are the numbers `deckster lint` holds it to; `coloredSeries` is the brand's categorical palette size, counted without series a highlight mutes.
